question: What does a correct program cost, in billed dollars, when a current low-cost model writes it in Python, Sley (Python dialect), C, Rust, Go or TypeScript?
primary_metric: dollars per correct program = billed spend on all attempts / programs passing all 128 hidden cases
secondary_metrics: billed input / cached / output tokens per trial

claude-haiku-5-5.prompt_cache: one 5-minute cache breakpoint at the end of the system block (shared text, plus the card on Sley); prefixes under 512 tokens are not cached by the API

claude-code-haiku-5-5.cli: claude -p --output-format json --model claude-haiku-5-5 --tools '' --system-prompt <harness system text> --effort low [--safe-mode --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config]
claude-code-haiku-5-5.retries: one prompt per call: earlier replies and feedback are carried as text
claude-code-haiku-5-5.calibration: one near-empty call per run measures what the CLI still adds to every prompt

attempts.retry_feedback: visible test or compiler output, truncated to 4,000 characters

output_cap_note: The cap includes reasoning tokens. A response stopped by the cap is a failed attempt (it still bills).
sley_card: The output of `sley-agent help python` is sent with every Sley attempt and billed; it is the start of the prompt so the provider can cache it.
prompt_order: shared system text, then (Sley only) the card, then the task; the shared prefix comes first for caching
oracle: 128 seeded cases per task (seed 218), edge cases first, from tasks.reference; independent of the visible tests and of any model
success: the final program passes the visible tests and all 128 hidden cases
exclusions: infrastructure failures (HTTP 5xx, timeouts, rate limits after retries, toolchain crashes) are recorded and shown, and excluded from the success denominator; refusals, truncations, syntax errors and wrong answers are failures

spend_guard.rule: before each call, reserve its worst-case cost (prompt + full output cap at list price); refuse the call if spent + reserved would pass the guard

held_out: max_subarray, count_leq, root_sum, clamp_sum (edit) and count_multiples (edit) were written after the token-loop benchmark; their statements are new but the problems are classic, so contamination is possible and is disclosed
publish: results.jsonl (every call, UTC-stamped, with billed usage), summary.json, summary.md, the price table with URLs and dates, and this file's SHA-256

amendments.change: Default models: gpt-6-luna replaced by claude-haiku-5-5 (Anthropic Messages API, Message Batches for first attempts, effort low) at the owner's request. gpt-6-luna moves to optional. No paid call had been made under the original registration, so no result is affected.

Optional model claude-code-haiku-5-5: Claude Haiku 5.5 through the Claude Code CLI, paid from Claude Code cloud-session credit at the owner's request. Its dollars are estimates at API list price, not billed per token, and its rows are labeled as such; it is not pooled with API-billed rows.

Oracle fix for collatz: with limit = 2 the only starting value is n = 1 (0 steps), so the statement's answer is 1, but the oracle and the six reference programs started the running best at 0 steps and returned 0. They now start it at -1. Only limit = 2 changes (hidden case 3 of 128, run in every trial). The first full-tier Claude Code run (2.1.8/claude-code-full) was scored with the old oracle, so its collatz rows failed in every language; they are re-scored with the fixed oracle and both scores are published.

Sley card: `sley-agent help python-task` replaces `help python`. It is the same dialect card without the lines on writing inline tests (`def test_*`, `pytest.raises`, assertions), which the prompt tells every model not to write, plus one line that only parameters and returns need types. It is a 2.1.8 change under test: the full-tier Claude Code run of 29 Oct (2.1.8/claude-code-full, `help python`) is the before measurement, and runs with the new card are published beside it, not pooled with it. The manifest records the card topic and SHA-256.
